proposed_comments.title: Reserve stdout as the JSON protocol channel
proposed_comments.body:
### Reserve stdout as the JSON protocol channel

**Severity:** `high`

Python-level redirect_stdout does not cover native extensions or subprocesses. Redirect file descriptor 1 while user code runs so their output cannot corrupt the JSON response.

```suggestion
@contextlib.contextmanager
def _redirect_all_stdout_to_stderr():
    """Redirect Python and native/subprocess stdout while user code runs."""
    saved_stdout_fd = os.dup(sys.stdout.fileno())
    try:
        os.dup2(sys.stderr.fileno(), sys.stdout.fileno(), inheritable=True)
        with contextlib.redirect_stdout(sys.stderr):
            yield
    finally:
        os.dup2(saved_stdout_fd, sys.stdout.fileno(), inheritable=True)
        os.close(saved_stdout_fd)


def _format_output(result, output_type: str) -> dict:
```

proposed_comments.title: Use descriptor-level isolation while importing the script
proposed_comments.body:
### Use descriptor-level isolation while importing the script

**Severity:** `high`

Script imports can execute native code or child processes before the conversion function runs. Use the descriptor-level context manager here as part of the same batched fix.

```suggestion
    with _redirect_all_stdout_to_stderr():
```

proposed_comments.title: Restore stdout only before emitting the final JSON
proposed_comments.body:
### Restore stdout only before emitting the final JSON

**Severity:** `high`

Formatting can also invoke user-controlled objects. Keep it inside the isolated region and emit the protocol result only after stdout has been restored.

```suggestion
    with _redirect_all_stdout_to_stderr():
        result = fn(input_value)
        output = _format_output(result, output_type)

    # Output JSON result after restoring the protocol channel.
```

Clamp persisted Python timeouts before millisecond conversion
proposed_comments.body:
### Clamp persisted Python timeouts before millisecond conversion

**Severity:** `high`

The timeout is later multiplied by 1000. Clamp the persisted seconds value so malformed settings cannot overflow that conversion.

```suggestion
                                PythonScriptTimeoutSeconds = pythonScripts.TimeoutSeconds > 0
                                    ? Math.Min(pythonScripts.TimeoutSeconds, int.MaxValue / 1000)
                                    : 30;
```

proposed_comments.title: Treat a null Python action list as empty
proposed_comments.body:
### Treat a null Python action list as empty

**Severity:** `high`

Deserialization may produce a null action list. Avoid failing the entire settings load when no saved script actions are present.

```suggestion
                                _pythonScriptActions.AddRange(pythonScripts.Value ?? []);
```

proposed_comments.title: Expose asynchronous trust persistence
proposed_comments.body:
### Expose asynchronous trust persistence

**Severity:** `high`

Trust persistence must not synchronously block the UI while the settings loader may be waiting for that same scheduler. Change the settings contract as part of the batched async conversion.

```suggestion
        Task StoreTrustedScriptHashAsync(string scriptPath, string hash);
```

proposed_comments.title: Persist trusted hashes outside the UI thread
Make the trust service contract awaitable
proposed_comments.body:
### Make the trust service contract awaitable

**Severity:** `high`

Propagate the asynchronous persistence contract through the trust service so callers cannot accidentally block on the settings lock.

```suggestion
    Task StoreTrustAsync(string scriptPath, string hash);
```

proposed_comments.title: Forward trust persistence asynchronously
Await trust persistence before execution
proposed_comments.body:
### Await trust persistence before execution

**Severity:** `high`

Await the asynchronous trust write so execution observes a durable decision without blocking the UI thread.

```suggestion
            await _pythonScriptTrustService.StoreTrustAsync(scriptPath, trustedHash);
```

proposed_comments.title: Reject pip option tokens in script metadata
proposed_comments.body:
### Reject pip option tokens in script metadata

**Severity:** `high`

The existing character allowlist accepts tokens beginning with a hyphen, allowing metadata to inject pip options. Require a distribution-name character first.

```suggestion
            .Where(token => System.Text.RegularExpressions.Regex.IsMatch(token, @"^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9\._\-\[\],>=<!=~]*$"))
```

### Persist Python settings repairs after loading

**Severity:** `high`

Track the migration result before the scheduled in-memory update, avoid rerunning migration inside that callback, and save when either AI or Python settings were repaired. The required insertion point is outside the current PR diff, so this coordination cannot be represented as a valid inline suggestion.

proposed_comments.title: Use output files for both WSL JSON protocol paths
proposed_comments.body:
### Use output files for both WSL JSON protocol paths

**Severity:** `high`

Both WSL execution paths need coordinated input/output-file framing so login-profile output cannot corrupt JSON. This spans several separated hunks in PythonScriptService.cs and should be applied as one implementation change rather than as a partial inline edit.

proposed_comments.title: Use one syntax-aware parser in runtime and Settings
proposed_comments.body:

Add a shared PythonSourceParser and use it for runtime discovery, dependency scanning, and Settings discovery, with matching regression tests. Because the parser is a new file not present in the current diff and the call sites are separated, GitHub cannot represent the complete change as one safe inline suggestion.

manual_test_instructions: In Settings, switch Python scripts among Off, Windows Python, and WSL Python; choose the scripts folder and interpreter; restart Settings and Advanced Paste and confirm the values persist.
Add named-function scripts for text, image, and files; verify names, descriptions, enabled state, and conversion summaries agree between Settings and the Advanced Paste window.
Run a script that prints from Python and from a child process and confirm the converted clipboard result remains valid JSON-backed output.
Copy one image file, multiple files, and audio/video files from Explorer; confirm eligible scripts receive the expected file_paths and dedicated media/image path.
Cancel import probes and package installation, exercise timeout behavior, and confirm no Python, pip, or WSL child process remains running.
Modify a trusted script during preparation and confirm execution fails closed; approve it again and confirm the new hash persists.
Use Narrator and keyboard navigation on the folder, interpreter, open-folder, and open-script buttons; verify the Advanced Paste window remains bounded on a 768-pixel-high display.
